preconditions.description: The number of rows in the garden is between 1 and 100.
The number of columns in the garden is between 1 and 100.
The total number of squares in the garden is at most 200.
The number of important squares is between 1 and the minimum of the total number of squares and 7.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a[i][j] <= 1000 for i in range(n) for j in range(m))
preconditions.description: Each square contains between 1 and 1000 flowers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= m for x, y in important_squares)
preconditions.description: Each important square's coordinates are within the garden's bounds.
All important squares have different coordinates.

postconditions.expression: all(garden[x-1][y-1] == 'X' for x, y in important_squares)
postconditions.description: All important squares are covered with concrete.

postconditions.expression: all(garden[i][j] in ['X', '.'] for i in range(n) for j in range(m))
postconditions.description: Each square in the garden is either covered with concrete or not.

postconditions.expression: all(is_connected(x1-1, y1-1, x2-1, y2-1, garden) for (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in itertools.combinations(important_squares, 2))
postconditions.description: There is a path of concrete-covered squares between any two important squares.

postconditions.expression: dead_plants == sum(a[i][j] for i in range(n) for j in range(m) if garden[i][j] == 'X')
postconditions.description: The total number of dead plants is the sum of flowers in all concrete-covered squares.
The output correctly reports the minimum number of dead plants.
The output correctly represents the garden's plan with 'X' for concrete-covered squares and '.' for uncovered squares.
